hypotheses.text: The recorded triple-dose fertilizer application may be associated with an elevated risk of fertilizer salt buildup or root-zone stress.
If leaf browning, yellowing, tip burn, or wilting are observed, those signs may be associated with fertilizer concentration stress, though other factors cannot be ruled out.
The plant may recover without intervention if the fertilizer dose was not excessive for its pot size, soil mix, and watering pattern.

followUpChecks: Inspect the plant now and over the next 7-14 days for leaf yellowing, brown tips, crispy edges, wilting, or new growth.
Check the soil surface and pot drainage for salt crust, soggy soil, or poor drainage.
If the pot drains well, consider gently flushing the soil with water to reduce fertilizer salts, then allow it to drain fully.
Pause additional fertilizer until new healthy growth is observed, then resume at a lower dose if needed.
Record photos of the whole plant and close-ups of affected leaves, along with pot size and watering notes.
Compare the plant with reliable Monstera care guidance before making further fertilizer changes.
Monitor for improvement or worsening over 2-4 weeks and adjust watering and light based on observed condition.
